title: Frobenius on coefficient twists
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ ($n\geq1$). Let $Y_0$ be a finite-type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k_0$-scheme (the case used most is $Y_0=\Spec k_0$, $Y=\Spec k$), $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and $g=g_Y:Y\to Y$ the geometric-Frobenius automorphism [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], an isomorphism of schemes; $\ell$ is invertible on $Y$. For $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$ let $\Lambda_Y$ be the coefficient object and $\Lambda(m)_Y$, $m\in\mathbf Z$, the Tate twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], built from $\Zl(1)_Y=\varprojlim_r\mu_{\ell^r,Y}$ [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf] by tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and inverse limits [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The *canonical Weil structure* (Frobenius) on the twists is defined as follows.

1. *Coefficient rings.* For $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E\}$ let $c_\Lambda:g^{-1}\Lambda_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_Y$ be the structure isomorphism of the inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] (for $\mathcal O_E$ the composite through $g^{-1}\varprojlim\cong\varprojlim g^{-1}$, as in [def-weil-constant-weil-structure] 2); likewise $c_{\Zl}$, $c_{\mathcal O_E}^{\mathrm{const}}$ for the constant sheaves $(\Zl)_Y$, $(\mathcal O_E)_Y$. Through $c_\Lambda$, inverse images $g^{-1}\mathcal M$ of $\Lambda_Y$-modules are regarded as $\Lambda_Y$-modules.

2. *The Tate line.* For $r\geq1$ let $c_{\mu_{\ell^r}}=c^{g}_{\mu_{\ell^r}}:g^{-1}\mu_{\ell^r,Y}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{\ell^r,Y}$ be the inverse-image comparison map of roots of unity [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image], an isomorphism compatible with the transition maps $u\mapsto u^\ell$ and semilinear over $c_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}$ [lem-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image-iso]. Put
$$
 \tau_{\Zl(1)}:g^{-1}\Zl(1)_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_rg^{-1}\mu_{\ell^r,Y}\xrightarrow{\varprojlim_rc_{\mu_{\ell^r}}}\Zl(1)_Y,
$$
the first arrow being the canonical isomorphism of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] 2, and
$$
 \tau^{\mathcal O_E}_1:g^{-1}\mathcal O_E(1)_Y\xrightarrow{\sigma}g^{-1}\Zl(1)_Y\otimes_{g^{-1}(\Zl)_Y}g^{-1}(\mathcal O_E)_Y\xrightarrow{\tau_{\Zl(1)}\otimes c^{\mathrm{const}}_{\mathcal O_E}}\mathcal O_E(1)_Y,\qquad
 \tau^{A_{E,n}}_1=\tau^{\mathcal O_E}_1\otimes c_{A_{E,n}}:g^{-1}A_{E,n}(1)_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{E,n}(1)_Y,
$$
where $\sigma$ (and below every identification of $g^{-1}$ of a tensor product or sheaf Hom) is the isomorphism of [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom]. Each $\tau^\Lambda_1$ is a $\Lambda_Y$-linear isomorphism.

3. *All twists, sheaf level.* For $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E\}$ put $\tau^\Lambda_0=c_\Lambda$; for $m\geq1$ let $\tau^\Lambda_m:g^{-1}\Lambda(m)_Y\cong(g^{-1}\Lambda(1)_Y)^{\otimes m}\xrightarrow{(\tau^\Lambda_1)^{\otimes m}}\Lambda(m)_Y$; and for $m<0$ let $\tau^\Lambda_m:g^{-1}\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_Y}(\Lambda(-m)_Y,\Lambda_Y)\cong\mathcal Hom(g^{-1}\Lambda(-m)_Y,g^{-1}\Lambda_Y)\to\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_Y}(\Lambda(-m)_Y,\Lambda_Y)$, $\varphi\mapsto c_\Lambda\circ\varphi\circ(\tau^\Lambda_{-m})^{-1}$. Each $\tau^\Lambda_m$ is a $\Lambda_Y$-linear isomorphism of sheaves.

4. *Derived level.* $\Lambda(m)_Y$, placed in degree $0$, lies in $D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, prop-weil-twist-preserves, lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible]. With the isomorphism $\lambda:Lg^*\Lambda(m)_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}g^{-1}\Lambda(m)_Y$ identifying the derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] along the isomorphism $g$ with the inverse image [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback], put
$$
 \theta^\Lambda_m=\tau^\Lambda_m\circ\lambda:Lg^*\Lambda(m)_Y\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda(m)_Y\quad\text{in }D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)\qquad(\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E\}).
$$
For $\Lambda=E$, $E(m)_Y$ is the image of $\mathcal O_E(m)_Y$ in $D^b_c(Y,E)=D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi_E]$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and $\theta^E_m=\theta^{\mathcal O_E}_m\otimes1$, its image; $E(m)_Y$ lies in the constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart], so $(E(m)_Y,\theta^E_m)$ is a constructible $E$-Weil sheaf, an object of $D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, the canonical Weil structure on $\Qlb(m)_Y$ is the object $(E,(E(m)_Y,\theta^E_m))$ of $D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,\Qlb)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], whose image under $\operatorname{For}$ is $(E,E(m)_Y)=\Qlb(m)_Y$. For $m=0$, $\theta^\Lambda_0$ is the canonical Weil structure of the constant coefficient object [def-weil-constant-weil-structure].

5. *Twist of a Weil complex.* For $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$ and a $\Lambda$-Weil complex $(K,\theta_K)\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,\Lambda)$, its twist is $(K,\theta_K)(m)=(K(m),\theta_{K(m)})$, where $K(m)=K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_Y}\Lambda(m)_Y$ [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], which lies in $D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ [prop-weil-twist-preserves], and
$$
 \theta_{K(m)}:Lg^*(K\otimes^L\Lambda(m)_Y)\xrightarrow{\ \mu_{g;K,\Lambda(m)_Y}\ }Lg^*K\otimes^LLg^*\Lambda(m)_Y\xrightarrow{\ \theta_K\otimes^L\theta^\Lambda_m\ }K\otimes^L\Lambda(m)_Y,
$$
with $\mu$ the isomorphism of derived pullback with derived tensor product [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]; it is an isomorphism, so $(K,\theta_K)(m)$ is an object of $D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. A morphism $u$ of Weil complexes gives the morphism $u\otimes^L\mathrm{id}$ of their twists.

The pairs $(\Lambda(m)_Y,\theta^\Lambda_m)$ are the twists with their natural Weil isomorphisms induced by the geometric-Frobenius convention. (That the resulting geometric Frobenius acts on $\Lambda(m)$ over $\Spec k_0$ by $q^{-m}$, compatibly with finite reduction and scalar extension, is a statement about this definition, lem-pur-twist-frobenius-scalar; it is not part of the definition.)

proof.text: Extend the canonical root-limit map first to the completed integral root line and then to each finite coefficient root line. Apply the proved generic positive-power transport theorem. At zero its unit formula is the specified completed coefficient map, or the constant scalar map in the finite case. At one the first-line normalization applies. Induct with the binary pure-tensor formula for every higher degree. To prove uniqueness, transpose two maps through the module adjunction and use root-power generator extensionality. This discharges both original positive-family existence-and-uniqueness obligations from four strictly smaller root statements.

For each negative degree transport internal Hom across the ringed site equivalence and conjugate by the positive map and degree-zero map. Its evaluation formula follows from the normalized internal-Hom comparison. To prove uniqueness, apply module adjunction injectivity and the full faithfulness of reindexing along the site equivalence; the positive map and adjunction unit are invertible, so evaluation on their images determines the negative map. Combine the disjoint nonnegative and negative integer cases.

Construct the normalized strict pullback augmentation. The completed coefficient maps used by the ringed-site and ordinary slice constructions agree by their finite projection equations. Uniqueness of left adjoints therefore identifies the module pullbacks, with the adjunction-unit normalization. Transport ordinaryQuotientAugmentation across this comparison. Its product is killed by 1-s, by naturality along consecutive quotient transitions. The mapping-cocone lift with zero second cochain gives a chain map. The coordinate formulas for the Roos map prove naturality. For uniqueness, product projections, degreewise module adjunction injectivity and equality on unit generators identify the first cone component; the prescribed zero second component and the mapping-cocone identity then determine the entire map.

Identify the assigned pullbackAugmentation with the explicit canonical tower augmentation by uniqueness and its already proved generator formulas. A generic mapping-cocone precomposition identity then identifies it with augmentationComplexComparison followed by ordinaryCompletionChain; product projections agree and both shifted coordinates vanish. On a good complete input, intrinsic/legacy completeness comparison and the proved complete_roosUnit lemma make the source roosUnit invertible after Q, using K-flatness of the given good representative. Exact ordinary pullback preserves this quasi-isomorphism. The strict reindexing comparison identifies its composite with the isomorphism of Roos complexes with ordinaryCompletionChain. The module pullback comparison is also an isomorphism, so Q of the original augmentation is invertible.

For the completed-to-ordinary comparison in clause 4, use the proved localization of flat-term K-flat complexes at quasi-isomorphisms. Compose the ordinary exact-derived-functor comparison, Q of the specified strict pullback augmentation, and the inverse normalized integral pullback comparison on good complexes. Fully faithful precomposition with this localization descends this composite to a natural transformation from ordinary to completed pullback on the entire derived category. Its pullback to good complexes is the original composite by map_preimage.

Restrict the descended transformation to integral constructible objects. Choose a good representative using essential surjectivity of localization. Integral constructibility transports along its representative isomorphism by sfIntegralConstructible_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms. The existing obligation pullbackAugmentation_isIso makes the component invertible on that representative; naturality transports invertibility to the original object. Invert this natural isomorphism. Cancellation of the three comparison factors identifies its components exactly with completedToOrdinaryOnGood. For uniqueness, two normalized isomorphisms agree on every good constructible representative; naturality and cancellation along the representative isomorphism show equality at every constructible object. The normalized augmentation invertibility is now proved from the strict reindexing comparison and the proved complete_roosUnit lemma. The positive sheaf-map obligations are now reduced to first-line transport and generator extensionality as in the first step.

The existing signed-power proof is packaged in the proved generic signed-power transport module, with the same internal-Hom conjugation and evaluation normalization. Apply it to the integral and finite positive comparisons; all original public specialization signatures are preserved.
Use the extracted existing generic argument: Incoming mapping-cocone coordinate extensionality. Its proof is unchanged and introduces no new mathematical obligation.

split_report.summary: Checked against Deligne, Weil II (1.1.7) pp. 150-151 (F = phi^{-1}), (1.1.14) p. 153, (1.2.5)(iv) p. 154 and (1.2.7) pp. 154-155, and Weil I (2.2) pp. 280-281 (Z_l(1) = lim mu_{l^n}, phi acts by q). The imported statement named no construction of the Weil isomorphism on Lambda(m) ('induced by the geometric Frobenius convention') and asserted, inside a definition, the statement that Frobenius acts by q^{-m}. Rewritten as the definition of the canonical Weil structure theta_m on Lambda(m)_Y for every finite-type Y_0 and every Lambda in {A_{E,n}, O_E, E, Qlbar}: from the roots-of-unity comparison map (new def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image, with new lem-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image-iso), the limit/tensor/Hom compatibilities of g^{-1} along an isomorphism (lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image, new lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom), and the derived identification lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback, in parallel with def-weil-constant-weil-structure; plus the twist of a Weil complex, (theta_K tensor theta_m) after the new lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso (prop-weil-operations, whose tensor lift would give the same, is not cited: its proof uses thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace, which uses this node, a cycle). The scalar claim (q^{-m}, compatibility with reduction and scalar extension) moved to the new statement lem-pur-twist-frobenius-scalar, which depends on this node; the roots-of-unity fact behind it is the new statement lem-pur-frobenius-roots-of-unity-power. def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties kept (finite type).
